novelty_basis: The asymptotics L(n) ~ phi^2 n are known (Cusenza et al.); an explicit O(log^2 n) error bound was not looked for in the literature.
proof_check: written proof (proofs/paper/C19.md Theorem 8 - the split phase reaches lazy(n) after Psi(lazy(n)) moves, so L(n) >= Psi(lazy(n)); then the weight identity a_(k+1) = phi^2 F_(k+1) + psi^(k+2) - k - 3); the argument is the Skeptic's (reviews/skeptic_C13_C19.md, C9), written out and checked by the Director; the bound holds on all 103,799 n of EXP-C19-05 (largest ratio 0.476)
statement: For every n, D(n) = B(n) - L(n) <= 1 + (t+1)(t+6)/2, where t is the top level of the lazy Fibonacci representation of n; consequently L(n) = phi^2 n - O(log^2 n). No optimality theorem is needed.
title: The deficit of the longest Zeckendorf game is O(log^2 n) - D(n) <= 1 + (t+1)(t+6)/2, so L(n) = phi^2 n - O(log^2 n)
